findings.title: Output from child processes escapes the in-process capture
quotes: then the helper returns that stdout, stderr and code n, as the subprocess did
findings.fix: compare `run_main` with the subprocess for a command that spawns a child, or capture at fd level

sources.situation: `tests/test_implement.py:nio` now calls `run_main` for commands such as `nio run` or the implement commands. `implement.py:24` shows these start child processes. A child inherits the real fd 1 and fd 2, so its output goes to the terminal and is missing from the returned stdout and stderr. An assertion on that output fails, or an expected-absent string is silently never seen. The three helper tests only compare `flow next` and `flow park`, so they cannot detect this.

findings.reason: implement.py:18 starts the test command with stdout=PIPE, so the CLI reads and prints the child's output itself and run_main captures it. `tests/test_implement.py:nio` is only called for `check tasks` (lines 591, 596). CT-1 keeps `tests/test_flow.py:nio` as a subprocess for the commands that spawn heavy children.

findings.title: Ctrl-C is swallowed as exit code 1
quotes: An uncaught exception gives 1 and its traceback on stderr.
findings.fix: re-raise `KeyboardInterrupt` after the `finally` restore, or catch `Exception` only

sources.situation: `except BaseException` in `run_main` also catches `KeyboardInterrupt`. The runner interrupts a long test, `cli` returns `(1, traceback)`, and the test run carries on or fails on a misleading assertion. The subprocess version propagated the interrupt, because the child died and the parent was still interrupted.

findings.title: AC-3 restore covers only four things, not the other state a shared process keeps
quotes: the test process's working directory, environment and `sys.argv` are as before the call, and no flow lock it took is left behind
findings.fix: assert `flow.HELD` is empty after a failing call, and say which other global state is out of scope

sources.situation: in-process calls share `flow.HELD` (keyed by the test's pid), `sys.modules` and imported-module globals, the umask and signal handlers. A CLI path that sets a module global or leaves an entry in `HELD`, for example after a hard failure before the `finally` at `flow.py:244`, leaks into the next test. `test_run_main_restores_process_state` only globs for `flow.lock` files. It never checks `flow.HELD`, which is what would make a later in-process "second holder" be treated as the first. The pid-alive stale check also behaves differently, because the lock holder is now always a live pid.

the lock assertion follows a `flow.record` stub that raises `RuntimeError` before any lock is taken, if the lock is taken inside `record`. If so, `assert not list((root / ".nio/specs" / S).glob("flow.lock"))` passes trivially. It does not show that a lock taken and then raised through is released.

findings.title: AC-1's 60 s and "results unchanged" claim has no observed evidence
quotes: then it finishes in under 60 s and every test result is unchanged
findings.fix: record the wall-clock of `tests/test_implement.py` at this commit and its per-test pass or fail against the base

sources.situation: the pack shows every test as `unknown`. The suite is "reused: the review of T-5 ran this suite at 72ca9e69". The three attack tests were "not run". A test that silently stopped asserting after the switch to `run_main` would go unnoticed. There is also no timing check, and `embed` is cached per process (CT-2), which can hide cold-load cost.

findings.title: No test measures the under-60-s runtime
quotes: then it finishes in under 60 s and every test result is unchanged.
findings.fix: have the human time `uv run python tests/test_implement.py` and record it, or add a timed check.

sources.situation: AC-1 is a human AC. The diff adds no test or check that times `tests/test_implement.py`. The pack's suite entry is a review reused from T-5, with no timing. Per-test results are unknown, so "every test result is unchanged" is also unconfirmed per test.

findings.reason: Plan.md:69 maps NFR-1 to "none" tests, and plan.md:77 says a test file can't time itself, so QS-1 is the measurement. TC-1 explicitly leaves "the time limit itself (under 60 s)" to QS-1. The tasks jury already refuted the same point (tasks J-3).

quotes: the `TextEmbedding` for a (model, cache folder) pair is built once per process instead of on every call
findings.fix: add a unit test that patches `fastembed.TextEmbedding`, calls `embed` twice, and asserts one construction.

sources.situation: `src/nio/index.py` gains `_model` under `functools.cache`. No added or changed test shows that two `embed` calls build one `TextEmbedding`, or that a different (model, cache) pair builds a new one. Only the suite-level result, which is unknown per test, touches this.

findings.reason: Plan.md:69 maps NFR-1/CT-2 to no test, and the tasks jury already refuted the same request (jury/tasks.md J-3). CT-2 fixes the cache key as (model, cache folder), which is what `functools.cache` on `_model(model, cache)` (index.py:46) does.

quotes: those tests still pass and still start a subprocess.
findings.fix: also cover the pid-lock, timeout and process-group tests, or spy on `Popen` in them as `test_cli_runs_in_process` does.

sources.situation: `test_isolated_tests_keep_a_subprocess` only checks that the function source contains `subprocess.run(`. It does not run the tests or watch a subprocess start. It would pass with a dead branch. Its regex over `test_implement.py` also covers only `test_nfr1_no_model_calls`. The AC names lock-held-by-another-pid, timeout and process-group tests, and none of those is checked.

findings.title: Process-isolation tests now run the CLI in-process
quotes: Given a test that needs process isolation (a lock held by another pid, a timeout, a process group), when it runs, then it still runs the CLI as a subprocess.
Tests that need their own process keep their own `subprocess.run` (FR-2, research RF-2).
findings.fix: keep the test's CLI call as a subprocess (for example a `subprocess.run` variant of `flow` for this test), and extend the guard to the timeout and process-group tests.

sources.situation: `test_ac49_time_limit` (tests/test_implement.py line 782) is a timeout and process-group test. It calls `flow(root, "red", S, "T-1", "--run", RUN)`, which now goes through `test_flow.cli` and `run_main` in the test process, not a subprocess. The guard `test_isolated_tests_keep_a_subprocess` checks only `test_cli_errors`, `test_nfr2_offline` and `test_nfr1_no_model_calls`, so this regression passes the guard unnoticed.

findings.reason: `test_ac49_time_limit` uses the shared `flow` helper, not its own `subprocess.run`, so it is not one of the RF-2 and TC-4 tests. Its timeout and process group belong to the test command that `implement.run` spawns in a child (implement.py:18), which stays a subprocess when the CLI runs in-process. FR-1 requires the shared helper to go in-process.
findings.where: tests/test_implement.py (`flow` helper, line 346 to 349; `test_ac49_time_limit`, line 782); tests/test_flow.py (`test_isolated_tests_keep_a_subprocess`, line 2331)

findings.title: A lock held by another pid is tested in-process
quotes: Given a test that needs process isolation (a lock held by another pid, a timeout, a process group), when it runs, then it still runs the CLI as a subprocess.
these tests start their own subprocess today, outside the shared helpers [research: RF-2]
findings.fix: call that CLI through a subprocess (`subprocess.run`), or state in AC-4 and CT-1 that a dead other pid is an in-process case and add the test to the guard's list if it is a subprocess case.

sources.situation: `test_` at tests/test_flow.py line 730 to 741 writes a stale lock with `old_lock(root, gone.pid, ...)`, where `gone` is a dead other pid, and then calls `cli(root, "park", S, "x")`. With the diff, that call runs in-process through `run_main`, not through a subprocess. AC-4 names "a lock held by another pid" as a case that must keep its subprocess, and the guard does not cover this test.

findings.reason: `test_ac56_stale_lock` goes through the shared `cli` helper, and CT-1 says `cli` calls `run_main` with no caller changes. The dead pid is a separate process the test itself starts. RF-3 says the lock check works in-process and only the pid-and-host check differs, and TC-4 lists the isolated tests, which do not include this one.
findings.where: tests/test_flow.py (the stale-lock park test, line 730 to 741, which calls `cli` at line 738)

findings.title: The 60-second limit on test_implement.py is not shown anywhere in the pack
quotes: then it finishes in under 60 s and every test result is unchanged

sources.situation: no test or check measures the wall-clock time of `tests/test_implement.py`. The pack's per-test results are all unknown and its only timing evidence is the suite's pass. The in-process helper and the model cache could both be right and the file still run over 60 s because of the other tests (the model is loaded once per process, but test_implement.py still starts many other subprocesses).
